business_summary: REC Ltd (Maharatna CPSU, Ministry of Power) lends across power generation, transmission, distribution and increasingly renewables, roads and other infrastructure; loan book Rs6.17 lakh cr (+Rs26,537cr in Q2 FY27). Funded mainly by AAA bonds. PFC holds ~52.6% (model knowledge) and the boards agreed a merger of REC into PFC at 88 PFC shares per 100 REC (RBI conditional NoC 2026-10-15). Q2 FY27 PAT Rs3,478cr (-21% YoY, higher expenses/provisions: Rs1,090cr vs Rs476cr); stock Rs297 hit a 52-week low on 2026-09-29; P/E 5.2, P/B 0.82, dividend yield 6.2%.

revenue_mix.segment: interest on renewable, infra and other loans

exposures.mechanism: +50bp credit cost on Rs6.17 lakh cr book = Rs3.1k cr pre-tax = Rs2.3k cr post-tax vs run-rate PAT Rs15.5k cr (TTM) => -15%; cycle persistence 0.4 and P/B 0.82 => -5. Starting NPAs are low and borrowers are mostly state-owned utilities (model), so tail only.

evidence.note: REC Q2 FY27: PAT Rs3,478cr (-21% YoY), second interim dividend Rs3.50, loan book +Rs26,537cr in Q2 to Rs6.17 lakh cr (CNBC TV18/Upstox/Sarkaritel)

+25bp 10y: benchmark for AAA PSU bond issuance (spread ~40-60bp, model) -> funding cost +6bp on 1-year refinancing + P/B 0.82 discount-rate effect: PAT -1% and multiple -0.5 => -1.5.

+25bp repo: ~25% of REC's liabilities are floating/bank-linked vs ~60% of assets floating (state utility loans reset) => NIM neutral-to-slightly positive short-run (+2bp) but market spreads widen; net -0.8 for demand/spread effects.

evidence.note: RBI MPC hiked repo 25bp to 5.50%, stance 'calibrated tightening' (Hindu/Reuters/CNBC TV18 headlines)
